podcast.body: Released in 1995, this song features a guitar riff similar to Chicago's "25 or 6 to 4" (1970) and Led Zeppelin's "Babe I'm Gonna Leave You" (1967). This similarity underscores the fact that guitar riffs are not protected by copyright. "That's Brain Stew from Green Day, right?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This 1995 song is cited as an example of a track featuring a guitar riff that cannot be copyrighted, and it is played as a precursor to similar riffs found in Chicago's "25 or 6 to 4" and Led Zeppelin's "Babe, I'm Gonna Leave You." "That's Brainstu from Green Day, right?"

podcast.body: This song had a B-side that initially appeared alongside it. This B-side later took on a life of its own, was re-recorded for the "Nimrod" album, and became one of Green Day's biggest hits. "Or a song like this, which was first found as a B-side to Brain Stew."
